name: SIRIUS
facts: It is the brightest star in the entire night sky.
It has a tiny companion star called 'The Pup' that is as heavy as the Sun but only the size of Earth.
Ancient Egyptians based their entire calendar on when this star rose in the morning.

name: CANOPUS
facts: It serves as a primary navigation guide for NASA spacecraft because it is so bright and located far from the equator.
It is 65 times wider than the Sun.
Ideally seen from the Southern Hemisphere; it never rises above the horizon for most of Europe.

name: RIGEL KENT
facts: This acts as the 'Sun' to the planet Proxima b, the closest known planet to our solar system.
It is actually a triple star system, with two bright stars and one faint red dwarf.
It is our closest stellar neighbor in the entire galaxy.

name: ARCTURUS
facts: It is moving across the sky at 122 km/s, faster than almost any other bright star.
It is an ancient star, likely born in a different galaxy that collided with the Milky Way long ago.
Its light was used to electronically open the 1933 Chicago World's Fair.

name: VEGA
facts: It spins so fast that it is shaped like an egg, not a sphere.
It was the North Star 12,000 years ago and will be again in the future.
Surrounded by a massive ring of dust and debris where planets might be forming.

name: CAPELLA
facts: It looks like one star, but it is actually four stars locked in gravity.
The two main stars are yellow giants that orbit each other every 104 days.
It is a source of X-rays, likely from magnetic activity between the stars.

name: RIGEL
facts: It is burning its fuel so fast it will explode as a supernova relatively soon.
It is illuminating the nearby Witch Head Nebula with its intense light.
Despite being 800 light years away, it shines brighter than stars that are 10 times closer.

name: PROCYON
facts: Its name means 'Before the Dog' because it rises just before Sirius.
It has a tiny, invisible companion star that is slowly dying.
It is one of the closest stars to Earth, practically in our backyard.

name: BETELGEUSE
facts: It is so huge that if placed in our solar system, it would swallow Mars and Jupiter.
It periodically dims and brightens as it 'breathes' and sheds dust.
It is expected to explode as a supernova, which will be visible during the day on Earth.

name: ACHERNAR
facts: It spins incredibly fast, flattening itself into a pumpkin shape.
Its equator is thousands of degrees cooler than its poles due to the spin.
The name means 'End of the River' in Arabic.

name: HADAR
facts: It is a pointer star to the Southern Cross.
It consists of two massive blue stars orbiting each other.
Ideally seen from the Southern Hemisphere.

name: ALTAIR
facts: It rotates fully in just 9 hours (our Sun takes 25 days).
It is one of the corners of the famous Summer Triangle.
Direct images of its surface show dark and light spots.

name: ACRUX
facts: The brightest and bottom-most star of the Southern Cross.
It is the standard for checking navigation in the southern sky.
Through a telescope, it splits into two distinct blue stars.

name: ALDEBARAN
facts: Known as the 'Eye of the Bull' in the Taurus constellation.
NASA's Pioneer 10 spacecraft is heading towards it (arrival in 2 million years).
It appears to be part of the Hyades cluster, but is actually much closer to us.

name: SPICA
facts: Two stars orbiting so close they distort each other into egg shapes.
They orbit each other every 4 days.
The primary star pulses like a beating heart, changing brightness slightly.

name: ANTARES
facts: Its name means 'Rival of Mars' because of its similar red color.
It is shedding matter so fast it is surrounded by a cloud of its own dust.
A massive star near the end of its life.

name: POLLUX
facts: It is the brighter of the Gemini twins, outshining Castor.
A planet named Thestias (2x Jupiter mass) orbits this star.
It is the closest giant star to Earth.

name: FOMALHAUT
facts: Known as the 'Lonely Star' because it sits in an empty part of the sky.
It looks like the 'Eye of Sauron' due to a massive debris ring around it.
One of the first star systems to have an exoplanet directly photographed.

name: DENEB
facts: One of the farthest stars visible to the naked eye.
It acts as the tail of the Swan constellation.
It will eventually explode as a supernova within a few million years.

name: MIMOSA
facts: The second brightest star in the Southern Cross.
It pulses rapidly, changing size and brightness every few hours.
It has a powerful stellar wind blowing at 2000 km/s.

name: REGULUS
facts: It spins so fast that if it spun 10% faster, it would fly apart.
It is actually a system of four stars bound together.
Because it sits on the ecliptic, the Moon frequently passes in front of it.

name: ADHERA
facts: One of the brightest sources of ultraviolet light in the sky.
Historically part of a group called 'The Virgins'.
It ionizes gas clouds light-years away with its radiation.

name: SHAULA
facts: This star marks the dangerous stinger of the Scorpion.
It is a triple star system.
It is young and emits strong X-rays.

name: CASTOR
facts: It looks like one star, but is actually six stars dancing together.
It consists of three pairs of binary stars.
It is the 'Mortal Twin' of Gemini.

name: GACRUX
facts: The top star of the Southern Cross.
It is the closest red giant to Earth.
Its orange color contrasts sharply with the other blue stars in the Cross.

name: BELLATRIX
facts: Known as the 'Amazon Star'.
It serves as Orion's left shoulder.
It was once thought to be further away, but is actually closer than Rigel.

name: ELNATH
facts: It marks the tip of the Bull's horn.
Historically, it was shared by both Taurus and Auriga constellations.
It has unusually high levels of Manganese.

name: MIAPLACIDUS
facts: It forms part of the 'Diamond Cross' asterism.
It has no known companion stars.
It rotates very quickly, completing a turn in under 2 days.

name: ALNILAM
facts: The center star of Orion's Belt.
It is losing mass 20 million times faster than our Sun.
Its intense light illuminates the molecular clouds around it.

name: ALNITAK
facts: The eastern star of Orion's Belt.
It sits right next to the famous Horsehead Nebula.
It is one of the hottest stars visible to the naked eye.

name: ALIOTH
facts: The brightest star in the Big Dipper.
It has a strange magnetic field that separates metals in its atmosphere.
It is 4 times larger than the Sun.

name: DUBHE
facts: One of the 'Pointer Stars' that helps find the North Star.
It is not part of the Dipper's family group, but just passing through.
It is a binary system with a smaller white companion.

name: MIRFAK
facts: It is moving through space with a large cluster of young stars.
It is 60 times wider than the Sun.
Binoculars reveal dozens of faint stars surrounding it.

name: WEZEN
facts: If it were as close as Sirius, it would shine as bright as the half-moon.
It is a massive star nearing the end of its life.
Its name means 'Weight' because it sits low in the sky.

name: SARGAS
facts: It is rapidly swelling in size as it ages.
Within a few million years, it will become a pulsating variable star.
It rotates very fast for a giant star.

name: KAUS AUS
facts: It represents the bottom of the Archer's bow.
It spins so fast it flings a shell of gas off its equator.
It has a faint companion star.

name: AVIOR
facts: It is invisible to observers in Europe and North America.
It is a rare eclipsing binary system.
It helped orient spacecraft during the Voyager missions.

name: ALKAID
facts: The star at the very tip of the Big Dipper's handle.
It is moving in the opposite direction to the rest of the Dipper.
It is one of the hottest stars visible to the naked eye.

name: MENKALINAN
facts: Two stars that constantly eclipse each other.
The stars are egg-shaped because they are so close together.
They are tidally locked, always facing each other.

name: ATRIA
facts: It is an 'Hybrid Star' with both hot and cool regions.
A navigational anchor for the southern sky.
It is 130 times wider than the Sun.

name: ALHENA
facts: It marks the foot of the Pollux twin.
It has just stopped burning hydrogen in its core.
An asteroid belt is suspected to orbit this star.

name: PEACOCK
facts: It rotates incredibly fast, likely preparing to explode.
It helps locate the celestial south pole.
It orbits a companion star every 11 days.

name: ALSEPHINA
facts: Part of the 'False Cross' which confuses sailors.
It is actually a triple star system.
One of the components eclipses the other regularly.

name: MIRZAM
facts: Its name means 'The Herald' because it rises before Sirius.
The entire star pulses like a beating heart every 6 hours.
It is a Beta Cephei variable star.

name: ALPHARD
facts: Known as the 'Solitary One' due to the empty sky around it.
It is enriched with Barium from a dead companion star.
It is 50 times wider than the Sun.

name: POLARIS
facts: It is the North Star, staying fixed while the sky rotates.
It is actually a triple star system.
It serves as a 'Standard Candle' to measure cosmic distances.

name: HAMAL
facts: A giant planet nearly 2x the mass of Jupiter orbits it.
Ancient astronomers used it to mark the Spring Equinox.
It is 14 times wider than the Sun.

name: ALGOL
facts: Known as the 'Demon Star' because it winks every 3 days.
A dimmer star passes in front of the brighter one.
Ancient Egyptians noted its variability on lucky/unlucky days.

name: DIPHDA
facts: It sits alone in a dim part of the sky.
It emits powerful X-ray flares, unusual for an old star.
It has exhausted its hydrogen fuel.

name: NUNKI
facts: The oldest named star, found on ancient tablets.
The Moon and planets often pass directly in front of it.
It is surrounded by interstellar gas.

name: ALPHECCA
facts: The 'Jewel' of the Northern Crown.
It is an eclipsing binary system.
A disk of dust orbits the pair, like a solar system in making.

name: SCHEDAR
facts: The bottom-right star of the 'W' shape.
It is a very stable star with few starspots.
It is 42 times wider than the Sun.

name: ASPIDISKE
facts: A rare type of white supergiant.
It will likely become a variable star soon.
It is 43 times wider than the Sun.

name: SUHAIL
facts: It creates shockwaves in its own atmosphere.
It will eventually explode as a supernova.
It is 210 times wider than the Sun.

name: CAPH
facts: It rotates once a day, flattening it into a pumpkin shape.
It is evolving from a white star into a red giant.
It is a Delta Scuti variable star.

name: RUCHBAH
facts: It eclipses its partner star periodically.
A disk of debris orbits the system.
Likely has asteroid collisions happening right now.

name: SEGIN
facts: A massive blue giant at the end of the 'W'.
It is 6 times wider than the Sun.
It marks where the Fall Equinox will be in the future.

name: MERAK
facts: One of the Pointers to the North Star.
It is surrounded by a disk of warm dust.
Planets may be forming there right now.

name: PHECDA
facts: Surrounded by a gaseous envelope.
It is spinning rapidly and blowing its atmosphere away.
Physically linked to the Mizar system.

name: MEGREZ
facts: The dimmest star in the Big Dipper.
It connects the handle to the bowl.
It is the lightweight of the group at only 1.6 solar masses.

name: MIZAR
facts: The first binary star ever discovered by telescope.
It is actually a quadruple star system.
Together with Alcor, it forms a sextuple system.

name: ALCOR
facts: The 'Rider' sitting on the horse (Mizar).
Used as an eyesight test by ancient armies.
It has a faint red dwarf companion.

name: KOCHAB
facts: It served as the North Star in 1500 BC.
A gas giant planet 6x heavier than Jupiter orbits it.
It is a 'Guardian of the Pole'.

name: PHERKAD
facts: A shell star throwing off gas.
It varies slightly in brightness.
It forms a pair with Kochab called the Guardians.

name: MINTAKA
facts: The western star of Orion's Belt.
One star eclipses the other every 5.7 days.
It is a complex multiple star system.

name: SAIPH
facts: Orion's right knee.
It is as hot as Rigel but appears dimmer.
It emits most of its light in invisible ultraviolet.

name: GRAFFIAS
facts: A system of at least six stars.
The Moon often passes in front of it.
Jupiter eclipsed this star in 1971.

name: DSCHUBBA
facts: It unexpectedly flared in brightness in the year 2000.
It throws off disks of plasma.
It is a very energetic variable star.

name: WEI
facts: It helps form the curve of the Scorpion's tail.
It is an important source of X-rays.
It varies slightly in brightness.

name: LESATH
facts: Located right next to the stinger star, Shaula.
Together they are called the 'Cat's Eyes'.
It is evolving towards becoming a giant.

name: ALGIEBA
facts: A binary system visible in telescopes.
A massive planet orbits the main star.
Located in the Lion's mane.

name: ZOSMA
facts: Located on the hip of the Lion.
It is rotating very fast at 180 km/s.
It shares a common origin with the Big Dipper stars.

name: ALBIREO
facts: The most beautiful double star in the sky.
One star is bright gold, the other deep blue.
Astronomers debate if they are truly linked or just aligned.

name: SADR
facts: The heart of the Northern Cross.
Surrounded by a complex nebula.
It illuminates the gas clouds around it.

name: GIENAH
facts: Marks the wing of the Swan.
It is fusing helium in its core.
A stable star in its old age.

name: MARKAB
facts: The 'Saddle' of the winged horse.
It has a disk of debris around it.
It will become a red giant soon.

name: SCHEAT
facts: It varies irregularly in brightness.
A strong wind blows its outer layers into space.
It is 95 times wider than the Sun.

name: ALPHERATZ
facts: Its atmosphere has clouds of mercury and manganese.
The air is very still with no mixing.
It connects the Great Square of Pegasus to Andromeda.

name: MIRACH
facts: Used as a guide to find the Andromeda Galaxy.
A 'Ghost Galaxy' appears right next to it in telescopes.
It is 100 times wider than the Sun.

name: ALMACH
facts: A stunning quadruple star system.
Telescopes show a gold giant and a blue companion.
The blue companion is itself a triple star.

name: MENKAR
facts: The name means 'Nostril' in Arabic.
It is fusing helium into carbon.
It is losing mass into space.

name: KAUS MEDIA
facts: The middle of the Archer's bow.
It has three dim companion stars.
Part of the local Gould Belt of stars.

name: KAUS BOREALIS
facts: The top of the Archer's bow.
It points towards the center of the galaxy.
An unseen companion makes it wobble.

name: ALNASL
facts: The arrowhead of the Archer.
It produces a strong solar wind.
It is moving towards the Galactic Center.

name: ASCELLA
facts: Part of the 'Teapot' asterism.
A binary system orbiting every 21 years.
They swing close and then far apart.

name: POLIS
facts: Ideally avoided due to extreme radiation.
The primary is eclipsed by a companion every 180 days.
Visible to the eye despite huge distance.

name: RUKBAT
facts: Designated Alpha, but far from brightest.
Surrounded by a debris disk.
Likely has asteroids orbiting it.

name: ANCAA
facts: A binary system with a short orbit.
The companion orbits every 10 years.
Currently in a stable phase.

name: ALUDRA
facts: A massive star nearing the end of its life.
It will explode as a supernova.
One of the most distant visible stars.

name: MULIPHEIN
facts: Located in the collar of the Great Dog.
It is a chemically peculiar star.
It has unusual surface elements.

name: FURUD
facts: A binary star system.
The companion is invisible to telescopes.
They orbit every 675 days.

name: RASALHAGUE
facts: Spins at 88% of break-up speed.
The poles are hotter than the equator.
The star is shaped like a pumpkin.

name: CEBALRAI
facts: The 'Shepherd's Dog'.
It varies in brightness.
A planet may be orbiting it.

name: SABIK
facts: Two white stars orbiting each other.
Their orbit is very oval-shaped.
They swing close and then far apart.

name: YED PRIOR
facts: Rich in Nitrogen.
Located near the celestial equator.
Surface is relatively cool.

name: MARFIK
facts: Name means 'The Elbow'.
An eclipsing binary star.
The light dips as they cross.

name: ETAMIN
facts: The 'Zenith Star' of London.
Passes directly overhead in London.
Will be the brightest star in 1.5 million years.

name: ALDERAMIN
facts: Will be the North Star in 7500 AD.
Rotates very quickly.
Magnetic braking has not slowed it yet.

name: ALFIRK
facts: Prototype of pulsating variable stars.
Iron causes the star to pulse.
Brightness changes every few hours.

name: ERRAI
facts: A binary system.
Home to planet 'Tadmor'.
Tadmor is 1.6 times heavier than Jupiter.

name: TARAZED
facts: Burning helium in its core.
Rich in Carbon-13.
Looks close to Altair but is far behind it.

name: ALSHAIN
facts: Similar to what our Sun will become.
Has a faint red dwarf companion.
Magnetic activity matches the Sun.

name: DENEB OKAB
facts: The 'Tail of the Eagle'.
Rotates at 200 km/s.
Flattened shape due to spin.

name: ROTANEV
facts: Name is 'Venator' spelled backwards.
A binary of two subgiants.
High metal content.

name: SUALOCIN
facts: Name is 'Nicolaus' spelled backwards.
A system of seven stars.
Produces a strong stellar wind.

name: ZUBENELGENUBI
facts: A wide binary easily split with binoculars.
Stars are 5,000 AU apart.
They move together through space.

name: ZUBENESCHAMALI
facts: Historically reported as green.
Green stars are an optical illusion.
It is a rapid rotator.

name: UNUKALHAI
facts: The heart of the Serpent.
Emits strong X-rays.
Has active magnetic loops.

name: VINDEMIATRIX
facts: The 'Grape Gatherer'.
Signaled wine harvest time in antiquity.
Moving rapidly through the galaxy.

name: PORRIMA
facts: Spectacular binary for telescopes.
Two nearly identical twin stars.
Orbit is highly elliptical.

name: COR CAROLI
facts: Has an incredibly strong magnetic field.
5,000 times stronger than Earth's.
Separates elements in its atmosphere.

name: IZAR
facts: Named 'The Most Beautiful'.
Bright orange giant with blue partner.
Striking color contrast in telescopes.

name: MUPHRID
facts: Rich in heavy elements.
Stellar neighbor to Arcturus.
Appears close to Arcturus in the sky.

name: ALKALUROPS
facts: A triple star system.
Secondary stars flare in brightness.
Caused by magnetic activity.

name: NEKKAR
facts: A flare star.
Emits bursts of X-rays.
Atmosphere is expanding.

name: SEGINUS
facts: A Delta Scuti variable.
Swells and shrinks physically.
Changes brightness every few hours.
